Humanity has always imagined the road to the stars from the perspective of the people who will eventually travel it. We imagine stepping through some impossible doorway and emerging beneath an alien sun. We imagine the distance between worlds finally defeated, entire galaxies transformed into neighborhoods, and the cold emptiness of space reduced to a minor inconvenience. But roads do not build themselves. Someone has to cross the distance first. Someone has to enter the darkness before there is a doorway through it. Someone has to spend thousands, millions, perhaps billions of years laying the foundation for a civilization they may never live to see. And when that civilization finally arrives, transformed by time into something its ancestors could not recognize, what does it owe the people who built the road?
